newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Deals keep coming.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Deals keep coming.

text.p: Brazilian corporates look set to continue unloading fresh paper on an already over-supplied Eurobond market, but the amount of new issues is beginning to pressure launch prices, debt watchers said.
"The market is flush with paper so it doesn't seem to be a good idea (to issue). But the paper keeps coming," said a Eurobond trader in Sao Paulo.

Over $1 billion in new Brazilian issues -- including a $500 million deal from Espirito Santo private power firm Escelsa -- were priced this week despite healthy supply and recent volatility in local stocks, which have pressured Brazilian Bradies and Eurobonds.
DEALS THAT MAY SURFACE OVER THE NEXT FEW WEEKS INCLUDE:
* Banco BCN's $150 million three-year Eurobond. The deal is being led by UBS and price talk is at 240 basis points over Treasuries.
* Investment bank Pactual is also expected to price at least $50 million in five-year bonds through Credit Lyonnais. The bonds were seen coming at a spread of between 310 and 330 bps.
* MRS Logistica consortium, led by steel firm CSN, is reportedly planning a two-tranche bond for $320 million in August. Bankers Trust has been tipped as lead manager but the bank has denied comment.
IN SECONDARY TRADE, spreads on recent issues widened five or 10 basis points while spreads in general tightened 10 to 15 bps, trader said.

Brazil's 8.875 percent global due 2001 led the way, narrowing to 165 bps from the 195 range at the beginning of the week. The upturn was attributed to a strong recovery in local stocks and reduced fears of a currency crisis.
Brazil's 10.125 percent 30-year global due 2027 also performed well, narrowing about 25 points to 375 bps.
The gush of new paper, however, put more pressure on bonds issued within the past two months, traders said.
Underperformers included Sao Paulo electricity company Cesp's 9.125 percent due 2004 (put 01) which widened to 320 bps from about 300 bps.
Steelmaker CSN's 9.125 percent due 2007 also suffered, widening to 335 bps. The bond priced in mid-June at a spread of 275 bps over Treasuries.
Traders said both bonds were seen attractive at these spreads.
THE FLOOD OF NEW PAPER is beginning to push up launch prices, Brazil debt watchers said.

Espirito Santo private power firm Escelsa's $500 million 10-year bond priced at 387 bps over Treasuries, considered on the wide side of recent issues (Cesp's 2007 priced at 280 bps over in June), but a fair price nonetheless.

Traders said the new price environment has led to talk that Eletrobras' $200 million 10-year bond, scheduled to come over the next few weeks, will not fetch the 250 bp spread sought by lead manager ABN Amro.
"They are not going to get 250 over when their other bond (Eletrobras eight-year due 2004) is trading at 270 over today," said a Eurobond trader in Sao Paulo.
